title: Cloud setup: make a GitHub repository and connect it

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
In Phone 1 you controlled the Claude on your computer from your phone. It didn't work when the computer was off.

This course has Claude work on a computer on the internet (the cloud), no computer of yours needed. Today is just the setup.

  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: an email address, a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher), and a web browser on your phone or computer
There's a lot of signing up and settings today, so a computer browser is easier. A phone browser works too.

New to GitHub? Try the 10-minute GitHub at a glance first.

steps.title: First, what's GitHub?
steps.html:
Claude in the cloud can't see the Practice folder on your computer, so files need to live in a folder on the internet. That folder is a GitHub repository.

GitHubA service that keeps files on the internet. Made for developers, but fine for notes too
RepositoryOne folder inside GitHub. Today you'll make a notes folder called my-notes
PrivateA repository only you can see. Always make it private

steps.title: Join GitHub
steps.html:
1. Go to github.com in a browser and tap Sign up.
  2. Choose an email, a password and a username (e.g. jane-kim).
  3. Enter the code emailed to you, and you're in.

Already have an account? Just sign in. A free account is enough.

check.q: Are you signed in to GitHub?

steps.title: If signing up doesn't work
steps.html:
• No code? Check your spam folder.
  • Username taken? Add a number or a hyphen (-).
  • If a puzzle (human check) appears, just take it step by step.

steps.title: Make a private repository called my-notes
steps.html:
1. On GitHub, tap + at the top right → New repository.
  2. Repository name: my-notes
  3. Choose Private. Really!
  4. Tick Add a README file. (Claude needs a first file to work with)
  5. Create repository.
steps.alt: Making a repository named my-notes, Private, with README ticked

check.q: Was my-notes created, with a Private label next to its name?

steps.title: If making the repository doesn't work
steps.html:
• No + on your phone? Try the menu (☰) at the top left → Repositories → New.
  • Made it Public by mistake? Repository Settings → bottom Change visibility → Private.

steps.title: Connect Claude to GitHub
steps.html:
1. Go to claude.ai/code in a browser and sign in with your Claude account.
  2. When it asks you to Connect GitHub, follow along and tap Authorize on the GitHub screen.
  3. If you land back on claude.ai/code, it worked.

You only do this once.

check.q: Did you authorize on GitHub and come back to claude.ai/code?

steps.title: If no connect prompt appears
steps.html:
• A free Claude account can't use the cloud. Check you're on Pro or higher.
  • Work (Team/Enterprise) accounts need an admin to turn on the GitHub connection.
  • If it's already connected, you go straight in. Move on to the next step.

steps.title: Install the Claude app on the private repository
steps.html:
For a private repository, the Claude GitHub app must be installed before Claude can get in.

  1. Go to github.com/apps/claude and tap Install (or Configure). claude.ai/code may also lead you to this screen.
  2. Choose Only select repositories and pick just my-notes.
  3. Install.
Don't choose All repositories. It's safest to let Claude into only the repositories it needs.
steps.alt: Installing the Claude app on just my-notes with Only select repositories

check.q: Can you see my-notes in the repository list on claude.ai/code?

steps.title: If my-notes isn't in the list
steps.html:
• Check you picked my-notes on the app install screen. You can change it in GitHub Settings → Applications → Claude → Configure.
  • Refresh the claude.ai/code page.

steps.title: 🎉 Phone practice 2 done! Cloud setup complete
steps.html:
You now have a notes folder on the internet where Claude can work without your computer.

Private GitHub repository my-notesconnectedClaude (claude.ai/code)app installedReady

Three things to remember

  1. Always make repositories Private.
  2. Install the Claude app on selected repositories only (my-notes).
  3. Never put passwords or account numbers in the repository.
